planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or early fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Albopicta emerges bright yellow in spring with a narrow green margin and gradually fades to solid green by midsummer heat.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, avoiding hot afternoon sun that accelerates the fading of its variegation. Albopicta is one of the oldest and most widely grown Hosta fortunei selections, emerging in spring with bright butter-yellow leaves rimmed by a narrow dark-green margin, a striking two-tone effect that gradually fades to solid green by midsummer as chlorophyll fills in the yellow centers. The medium-to-large, slightly corrugated leaves form a dense, vigorous mound, and pale lavender flowers rise on tall scapes in July. A dependable, long-established garden favorite, it multiplies readily and tolerates more sun and heat than many blue-leaved hostas, making it useful for lightening a shaded border early in the season.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Univittata bears narrow, twisted leaves with a broad creamy-white center stripe against a dark-green margin.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Univittata tolerates a bit more morning sun than most variegated hostas without significant leaf scorch. One of the oldest hosta cultivars still widely grown, Univittata bears narrow, twisted, wavy-margined leaves with a broad, irregular creamy-white to pale-yellow center splashed against a dark-green margin, a striking reversal of the more common white-edged variegation pattern. The undulating, almost corkscrew twist along the leaf blade gives the mound a restless, textural look distinct from flatter-leaved hostas. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in summer above the small-to-medium clump, which spreads steadily and is useful for edging shaded paths.

common_name: American Sweetheart Hosta (Blue-Green Heart-Shaped Leaf with Creamy Margin)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; American Sweetheart bears large, thick blue-green heart-shaped leaves with a wide creamy-white margin.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; American Sweetheart holds its variegation best with some protection from hot afternoon sun. Bred by Hans Hansen, this vigorous hosta forms large, thick-substanced, heart-shaped blue-green leaves edged with a wide, irregular creamy-white to pale-yellow margin that brightens as the season progresses. The bold, glossy foliage resists slug damage better than many thinner-leaved cultivars, and near-white flowers appear on tall scapes in summer above the mounded clump. A strong grower that quickly forms an impressive specimen, it is well suited as a focal point in a shaded border or large container.

common_name: Dorset Blue Hosta (Compact Rounded Blue-Leaf Tardiana Group Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dorset Blue forms a compact mound of thick, rounded, powder-blue leaves and holds its color best in cool spring weather.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dorset Blue develops its strongest powder-blue coloring in cool spring weather before the waxy bloom breaks down somewhat in summer heat. Bred by British hosta pioneer Eric Smith as part of the renowned Tardiana Group, Dorset Blue forms a compact, rounded mound of thick, rounded, intensely blue-gray leaves and has been used extensively as a breeding parent, passing its blue coloring and compact habit into numerous modern hosta cultivars. Near-white to pale lavender flowers appear on short scapes in summer, staying close above the tidy foliage mound. Its small stature makes it well suited to edging, rock gardens, or the front of a shaded border.

common_name: Joy Ride Hosta (Vigorous Blue-Green Wavy-Margined Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Joy Ride forms a vigorous mound of thick blue-green leaves with a distinctly wavy margin.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where it forms a vigorous mound of thick-substanced, blue-green leaves with a distinctly wavy margin inherited from its Hosta hypoleuca-derived breeding line. A modern blue hosta valued both as a garden plant and as a breeding parent, Joy Ride holds its blue-gray cast well into summer thanks to a durable waxy bloom, and its ruffled leaf edges add textural interest to the mounded clump. Pale lavender flowers rise on tall scapes in mid to late summer above the foliage. Established clumps are long-lived and need dividing only every several years; watch for slugs, the primary pest of hosta foliage.

common_name: Smoke Signals Hosta (Strongly Blue Corrugated Breeding-Line Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in consistent partial to full shade; Smoke Signals bears thick, heavily corrugated, intensely blue-gray leaves.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in consistent partial to full shade, since the heavy waxy bloom responsible for its strongly blue coloring breaks down more quickly in hot sun or inconsistent moisture. Smoke Signals bears thick, heavily corrugated, intensely blue-gray leaves and is valued as one of the strongest blue parents used in modern hosta breeding programs, passing its deep color and substance to well-known offspring such as 'Skywriter.' Pale lavender-purple flowers appear on scapes in summer above the dense, mounded clump. Mulch to conserve soil moisture and divide congested clumps only occasionally, as it is a relatively slow, steady spreader.

common_name: Fried Bananas Hosta (Narrow Gold Strap-Leaf Novelty Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Fried Bananas bears narrow, elongated, twisted gold-chartreuse leaves in a dense dwarf mound.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Fried Bananas holds its brightest gold color with a bit of filtered morning sun. A dwarf novelty hosta related to the popular 'Curly Fries,' Fried Bananas bears narrow, elongated, strap-shaped leaves in bright chartreuse-gold that curl and twist along their length, forming a low, dense, spidery mound quite unlike typical broad-leaved hostas. Pale lavender flowers rise on short scapes in summer just above the foliage. Its small, tidy size makes it well suited to shaded rock gardens, container plantings, and the front edge of a mixed shade border; watch for slugs, the primary pest of hosta foliage.

common_name: Dolce Creme Brulee Heuchera (Golden Amber Ruffled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Dolce Creme Brulee is a Proven Winners introduction with warm amber-gold, caramel-toned ruffled foliage in a compact mound.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with some morning sun to develop the richest color; Dolce Creme Brulee is a Proven Winners introduction in the Dolce series, bearing ruffled, rounded leaves in warm amber-gold to caramel tones that deepen with cooler autumn temperatures. Its compact, mounded habit stays neat and tidy, making it well suited to shaded containers, edging a path, or as a warm-toned accent among cooler purple or green companions in a mixed border. Small cream-white flower spikes rise above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the warm leaf color. Provide consistent moisture and sharp drainage, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
